title: Valid Anagram
statement: You get two strings of lowercase letters. Return true if the second one can be made by rearranging the letters of the first, using every letter exactly as many times as it appears. Otherwise return false.

example.caption: Both words use one r, one a and one t. Only the order differs, so every count ends at zero.

idea.sentence: Count the letters of the first word going up, then the letters of the second word going down. Anagrams end with every count at zero.

jargon.plain: A word made by rearranging the letters of another word.
A table of letter to count. It is a small hash map.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: two lowercase strings, e.g. "anagram", "nagaram"

rows.name: Sort both strings
rows.note: Anagrams sort to the same string. Sorting costs the log factor.

rows.name: Tally up and down
rows.note: Two passes. The tally has at most 26 letters, so it does not grow with n.

fast.takeaway: Order does not matter for an anagram, only the counts do. Counting skips the sort.

stages.title: Length check, empty tally
stages.note: Different lengths fail at once. Otherwise start a table of letter counts.

stages.title: Count up with s
stages.note: Add one to the count of each letter of the first word.

stages.title: Count down with w
stages.note: Take one away for each letter of the second word. A count below zero means w has a letter s lacks.

stages.title: All zero
stages.note: Equal lengths and no negative count means every count is zero. It is an anagram.

edges.title: Two empty strings
edges.why: No letters on either side. Every count is trivially zero.

edges.title: Different lengths
edges.why: The length check answers at once. Without it, the leftover letter would need extra logic.

edges.title: Same letters, other counts
edges.why: Both use only a and b. The counts differ, so a set of letters is not enough.

edges.title: One letter
edges.why: Up one, down one, back to zero.

gotchas.text: The sort-both approach is tempting: [...s].sort().join('') === [...w].sort().join(''). It works for letters, but it is O(n log n). Array.sort with no comparer compares as text, so never reuse it for numbers.
Map.get returns undefined for a letter never counted. Use ?? 0, or the first increment gives NaN.
count[s[i]-'a'] panics if a byte is not a lowercase letter. An uppercase letter or a digit gives an index outside 0..25. For unicode input use map[rune]int and range over the string.
A [26]int is a value, not a pointer. It lives on the stack and is zeroed for you. No make call is needed.
Comparing only the sets of letters is wrong. "aab" and "abb" share the same letters with different counts.

recap.key: Anagrams have equal letter counts. Add for one string, subtract for the other, and nothing may go below zero.
recap.complexity: Time O(n). Space O(1) for 26 letters.
moves: Return false if the lengths differ
Subtract each letter of w. Below zero means false
